channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: IMF Projects Tajikistan's Economy to Grow by 7.3% in 2026
item.description: The International Monetary Fund forecasts Tajikistan's economy to grow by 7.3% in 2026, one of the highest rates in the Caucasus and Central Asia. Higher growth is projected for Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan. Regional economic prospects remain dependent on Middle East conflict consequences. The IMF noted that favorable commodity prices, remittances, and ongoing reforms contribute to regional economic stability.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Fire destroys roof of apartment building in Kentau, 32 evacuated
item.description: The roof of a three-story residential building in Kentau, Turkistan region, Kazakhstan, caught fire and was extinguished over a 250 square meter area. Thirty-two people, including seven children, were evacuated by rescuers. No injuries were reported as a result of the incident.

item.title: Russia's Lavrov Warns of Militants Infiltrating Central Asia from Afghanistan
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that militants from international extremist groups are attempting to enter Central Asian countries from Afghanistan, using both legal and illegal channels. He noted particular activity in Afghan areas bordering Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, with potential infiltration disguised as refugees or tourists. Russia's special services identify the 'Vilayat Khorasan' group as a primary threat.

item.title: Russian Missile Strikes Hit Kharkiv and Dnipro, Causing Casualties and Damage
item.description: Russian forces launched missile attacks on Kharkiv and Dnipro on the evening of October 16, resulting in fatalities and injuries. Residential buildings were damaged in Kharkiv, with local authorities reporting significant destruction. This marks the latest in a series of strikes on the city, which has seen multiple casualties in recent weeks.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Financial Support for Entrepreneurs at Business Forum
item.description: A panel session on banking and insurance solutions for businesses was held in Tajikistan as part of the "Tajikistan, Forward!" entrepreneurs' forum. Participants discussed access to financing, digital services development, payment infrastructure expansion, and insurance market opportunities. The event was initiated by the National Bank of Tajikistan.

item.title: US Limits Starlink Access for Ukraine, Raising Concerns Over Military Communications
item.description: The United States has temporarily restricted Ukraine's military access to Starlink satellite internet, a crucial system for drone and troop command. This move raises questions about potential communication disruptions for Kyiv and whether Europe can offer viable alternatives. The implications for Ukraine's defense capabilities are significant.

item.title: Mysterious Death of 62-Year-Old Man in Istaravshan, Wife Hospitalized
item.description: A 62-year-old man died under mysterious circumstances in Istaravshan, with his wife hospitalized. The incident occurred on the night of October 10 in Bobotagho village. The exact cause of death is unknown, and prosecutors are investigating. The man's body showed stab wounds.

item.title: Trump Lifts New Sanctions and Tariffs Against Russia
item.description: US President Donald Trump has canceled new sanctions and tariffs against Russia, which were scheduled to take effect this week. Reuters reported that Trump prevented the implementation of these measures by issuing an executive order. The White House stated the cancellation serves US national interests.

item.title: Over 2 Kilograms of Drugs Seized in Surxondaryo; Enough to Poison 8,124 People
item.description: Over two kilograms of narcotic drugs were found in a citizen's home in Surxondaryo. According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the seized amount is sufficient to poison 8,124 people. A criminal case has been initiated regarding the incident.

item.title: Astana Resident Sentenced to 10 Days Arrest for Harassing a Woman
item.description: A resident of Astana has been sentenced to 10 days of administrative arrest for harassing a woman in public places. The court found the man guilty of petty hooliganism after he persistently demanded her phone number and made indecent gestures while intoxicated.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enacts Law on Presidential Immunity and Administration Officials
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law establishing criminal liability for violating the immunity of presidential administration officials and other state representatives. The law, effective October 15, extends lifelong immunity to the president, administration officials, and their family members. Immunity for administration leadership personnel lasts five years post-employment.

item.title: Islom Madaminov Appointed Deputy Governor of Fergana Region
item.description: Islom Madaminov has been appointed as the Deputy Governor of the Fergana Region. Prior to this appointment, he served as an advisor at the Embassy of Uzbekistan in Saudi Arabia. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Tajik Parliament Approves Construction of Antimony Processing Plant for $35 Million
item.description: Tajik lawmakers have approved the construction of an antimony processing plant with an investment of $35 million. The facility is projected to process over 150,000 tons of ore annually. This development aims to enhance the country's industrial capacity in mineral processing.

item.title: North Korea Claims Successful Test of AI-Powered Torpedo
item.description: North Korea announced it has successfully tested a new high-precision torpedo named 'Zam-2.0', utilizing artificial intelligence technology. The underwater test on October 15 aimed to verify improvements in the torpedo system's technical capabilities, including target identification and guidance.

item.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Claims Attack on Houthi Arms Smuggling Operations
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition claims to have attacked Houthi arms smuggling operations attempting to bring weapons by sea into Yemen's Hudaydah province. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki stated the operation targeted illicit arms transport. Fighting between the coalition and Houthis continues elsewhere in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explains How Citizens Can Correct Errors in Social Benefit Eligibility System
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Labor and Social Protection, Bakhtiyarazykpayev, addressed concerns about artificial intelligence errors affecting social benefit eligibility. Citizens can update their personal information via eGov or eGov Mobile. For discrepancies like incorrect marital status or non-existent registered vehicles, individuals should contact relevant ministries.

item.title: ADB Plans to Allocate $500 Million for Rogun Hydropower Plant in Tajikistan
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) plans to provide $500 million in financing for Tajikistan's Rogun Hydropower Plant, comprising a $200 million grant and a $300 million concessional loan. This was discussed during trilateral negotiations in Bangkok involving Tajikistan's Finance Minister, the World Bank, and the ADB, focusing on coordinating efforts for timely project implementation.

item.title: Uzbekistan to plant 140 million saplings in autumn as part of "Green Space" project
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to plant 140 million saplings in the autumn of 2026 as part of the national "Green Space" project. The initiative aims to increase greenery and combat desertification, following a presidential decree. Planting schedules vary by region, starting November 1st.

item.title: Trump temporarily suspends sanctions on Russian oil imports, easing tariffs for some countries
item.description: US President Donald Trump has temporarily halted sanctions that would impose up to a 500% tariff on countries importing Russian oil. This decision impacts plans to increase pressure on Russia and relations with China, India, and Turkey. The measures are not permanently removed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's branch of Moscow State University celebrates 25th anniversary, receives presidential congratulations
item.description: The Kazakhstan branch of Lomonosov Moscow State University celebrated its 25th anniversary. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated the institution, highlighting its contribution to science, education, and bilateral cooperation. Russian President Vladimir Putin also sent congratulations, noting the branch's role in strengthening ties.

item.title: Russian Deputy Prime Minister to Visit Afghanistan for Economic Cooperation
item.description: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk will lead a high-level economic delegation to Afghanistan. The visit aims to focus on trade and economic cooperation between Russia and the Taliban-controlled country. Russia is seeking to expand commercial ties, noting a doubling of financial turnover in the first half of the year. The exact travel date was not announced.

item.title: Pakistan CTD Claims Killing Mastermind Behind Kohat Police Center Attack
item.description: Pakistan's Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) claims to have killed Zahid Gul, the alleged mastermind behind a car bombing at the Kohat Police Lines. Gul, identified as a member of the Hafiz Gul Bahadur group, was reportedly killed in an operation in Lakki Marwat district. The attack in Kohat killed 17 police officers and six civilians.

item.title: Almaty to Upgrade Worn-out Heating Networks and Overloaded Substations Under National Project
item.description: Almaty will upgrade its worn-out heating networks and overloaded electrical substations as part of the "Modernization of Energy and Communal Sectors" (MECS) national project. This initiative aims to improve heating and electricity supply reliability, reduce outages, and create capacity for new consumers. The project includes reconstructing a major heat pipeline that has been in operation since the 1980s.

item.title: Iranian Navy Reports Oil Tanker Explosion in Strait of Hormuz Due to Sea Mine
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps announced a major explosion on another oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, reportedly caused by a sea mine. The tanker was carrying two million barrels of crude oil and was allegedly attempting to pass through an unauthorized route with its navigation systems disabled. Maritime authorities report a high number of attacks on vessels in the region.

item.title: Putin Orders Widespread Attacks on Ukraine's Logistics and Defense Hubs
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered widespread and coordinated attacks against Ukraine's defense facilities and logistics hubs. He stated that expanding these strikes is necessary for the ongoing "special military operation." This directive follows recent calls for an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, despite which Moscow continues its intense attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbekistan to prosecute individuals who assault presidential administration staff
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce criminal penalties for those who assault employees of the presidential administration. The new legislation aims to protect state officials and ensure the smooth functioning of government operations.

item.title: Trump Freezes Sanctions Against Russia Under "Graham Law" Set to Take Effect October 18
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has frozen anti-Russian sanctions mandated by the "Graham Law," which were scheduled to take effect on October 18. The order suspends tariffs of up to 100% on goods from major energy importers from Russia and 500% tariffs on Russian goods. These sanctions will remain suspended until further presidential determination.

item.title: Australian Citizen Detained in Immigration Facility for Nearly Three Years Due to Government Error
item.description: An Australian citizen was mistakenly held in an immigration detention center for 945 days due to a government error, which classified them as a foreigner. During this period, authorities attempted to deport the individual. The case highlights a significant administrative failure leading to prolonged unlawful detention.

item.title: Two Forest Fires Registered in Northern Kazakhstan Within 24 Hours
item.description: Two forest fires were detected within the state forest fund of Kazakhstan on October 16, 2026, both occurring in the North Kazakhstan region. Forest protection officers identified the blazes during ground patrols. Rapid response efforts contained and extinguished the fires before they could spread extensively.

item.title: Central Asian Leaders Praised with Cult of Personality, Study Finds
item.description: A study examines the phenomenon of personality cults in Central Asia, where leaders are consistently lauded as "wise," "great," and "worthy." The practice involves creating elaborate praise through songs, poems, and public declarations, often diminishing former leaders once a new one takes power. This analysis explores how such cults are formed and why public figures engage in excessive praise.

item.title: Ministers from Turkic States Convene in Astana to Strengthen Media Cooperation
item.description: Ministers and senior officials responsible for media from Turkic states held their 8th meeting in Astana. The gathering, part of the Astana Media Week international forum, focused on enhancing cooperation in the information sector. Discussions included combating deepfakes, verifying information, strengthening national news agencies, and improving journalists' digital skills.

item.title: Nine Kazakh Citizens Evacuated from Ukraine Conflict Zone to Russia
item.description: Nine Kazakh citizens found in the Ukraine war zone have been brought to Voronezh, Russia. A lawyer assisting their families confirmed the evacuation, initially reporting seven individuals and later updating to nine. Kazakh diplomats are negotiating with Russian authorities for their return home. The Foreign Ministry previously urged citizens to report relatives in combat zones.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Building Second and Third Nuclear Power Plants
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering the construction of not only a second but also a third nuclear power plant, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. He stated that negotiations with new investors for the second plant are scheduled. Mirziyoyev emphasized the importance of nuclear energy for guaranteed electricity supply and reduced costs, noting significant investments in uranium production.

item.title: Iranian War Thriller Screened at Tajikistan Film Festival
item.description: An Iranian thriller depicting a cyberattack on a bank during a 2025 war is featured at Tajikistan's Toji Somon National Film Festival. The film, "The Gambler," directed by Mohsen Bahari, is among several Iranian movies promoting cultural cooperation between Iran and Tajikistan. It has previously won awards at international festivals.

item.title: Starlink Services for Ukraine Reportedly Restricted, Musk Points to US
item.description: Ukraine has reported restrictions on Starshield, the military version of Starlink, impacting drone use and logistics. While media sources suggest the White House or Elon Musk initiated the restrictions, Donald Trump denies involvement. The Ukrainian Ministry of Defense confirmed service restoration in field conditions, but speed limits reportedly persist.

item.title: New School Uniform Rules in Azerbaijan Spark Protests Over Hijab Ban
item.description: Parents and students in Azerbaijan are protesting new school uniform regulations after reports of girls wearing hijabs being denied entry to classes. The amendment prohibits clothing not conforming to uniform requirements or contradicting secular education principles. While the hijab isn't explicitly mentioned, school administrations are interpreting the rules, leading to protests and detentions.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Meets Voltamp Energy Chairman to Discuss Solar Power Projects
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Sayid Ayman al-Busaidi, Chairman of Oman's Voltamp Energy. The meeting, held during the first Investors Council session for the fuel and energy sector, focused on developing mutually beneficial cooperation, including the construction of solar power stations and high-voltage transformer production. Agreements were reached on implementing current and new projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses Energy Projects with Leading Chinese Companies
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with executives from leading Chinese companies CAMCE, China Energy, and Sinoma Energy on the sidelines of the Investors Council meeting for the fuel and energy sector. Discussions covered joint projects in renewable energy, energy storage, waste processing, and water supply. Initiatives for a logistics hub in Andijan region, agrivoltaics, and oil and gas projects were supported.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Meets Aksa Enerji Chairman to Discuss Energy Sector Modernization
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Cemil Kazanci, Chairman of Turkey's Aksa Enerji, during the first Investors Council meeting for the fuel and energy sector. The discussion focused on expanding mutually beneficial cooperation, including the company's participation in projects for the development and technological modernization of Uzbekistan's energy sector. The parties agreed to accelerate work on specific projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan, Russia, Uzbekistan Disrupt Afghan Drug Smuggling Route, Seize 30kg Hashish
item.description: Security services of Kazakhstan, Russia, and Uzbekistan have disrupted a drug smuggling channel from Afghanistan via the "Northern Route." Two international drug traffickers were detained in Tyumen, Russia, with 30 kg of Afghan hashish seized, estimated at $300,000 on the black market. Pre-trial investigations are ongoing, and efforts to counter drug trafficking continue.
